title: GMP water system service plans and spare parts | Aquemi
meta: Service plans with stated response times, calibration to USP <645> and <643>, like-for-like spares and service reports fit for your GMP records.
eyebrow: SERVICE PLANS · CALIBRATION · SPARE PARTS · EU GMP ANNEX 15 · USP <645> · USP <643>
headline: Service that keeps your water system running and keeps it qualified
lead: Most water systems fall out of their qualified state on a maintenance day, not on a design drawing: a membrane of a different model, a calibration certificate nobody filed, a visit that never went through change control. Our service plans state the response time for each severity of fault, from [severity 1 on-site response time, hours] for a critical fault, and fix the scope in writing. Every visit runs under your change control and maintenance procedures, calibrations meet USP <645> (cell constant known to ± 2 %) and USP <643> (system suitability 85–115 %), and the signed service report is written to go straight into your good manufacturing practice (GMP) records.

blocks.h: Your water passed PQ. Service decides whether it stays that way.
body: After performance qualification (PQ), the qualified state of a Purified Water (PW) or Water for Injection (WFI) system depends on what happens to it every month: which parts go in, who calibrates the instruments and against what, how a fault at 2 a.m. gets fixed, and whether the record of all of it survives an inspection. 21 CFR 211.67 and 211.68 require equipment to be maintained and instruments calibrated to a written programme, with records. EU GMP Chapter 3 asks that repair and maintenance present no hazard to product quality and that control equipment be calibrated at defined intervals. In Canada, section C.02.005 of the Food and Drug Regulations, as Health Canada interprets it in GUI-0001, expects the same.

So we sell service as a defined product, not a phone number. Each plan states its response times, visits, calibrations, spares and reports before you sign, and every task inside it is written to work with your procedures: work orders raised in your maintenance system, parts replaced like for like or routed through your change control under EU GMP Annex 15, section 11, and calibrations with certificates traceable to national standards. When something does change the system, we tell you which part of the requalification it touches. See commissioning and qualification for how that scope is set.

blocks.h: What a preventive maintenance visit covers
blocks.intro: The task list for your system is written from its design and qualification records and agreed with you before the first visit. A typical PW or WFI visit includes the following.

items.t: Data review before any wrench is turned
items.d: Conductivity, TOC, temperature, flow and alarm history since the last visit, reviewed with your team, so the work answers the trend.

Normalized permeate flow, salt passage and differential pressure to ASTM D4516, compared with the commissioning baseline. Cleaning recommended at the membrane maker's trigger, typically a 10 to 15 % change.
Softener hardness leakage and regeneration, carbon bed or bisulfite performance, total chlorine at the RO inlet, silt density index (SDI) where your feed calls for it.
Replaced on the documented interval or on condition, like for like, with part numbers and lot numbers recorded.
Cartridge changes on differential pressure or interval; hydrophobic vent filters integrity tested to the filter maker's limits.
Lamp hours and intensity, sleeve condition, ozone generator output and ozone below the release limit after the destruct UV.
The hot water, steam or ozone cycle checked at its coldest or weakest point, with temperature and hold time, or ozone concentration, recorded.
Return flow against the qualified minimum, pump condition, heat exchanger performance and point-of-use valve condition.

blocks.h: Questions maintenance, validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Will service work affect our qualified state?
items.a: Not when it is maintenance done like for like under your procedure: same part, same specification, return-to-service checks, record filed. Anything else goes through your change control first. We classify every part we replace in the report, and where something is not like for like we stop and give you the input for the change request, including the IQ, OQ or sampling we would propose. See commissioning and qualification for how requalification scope is set.

items.q: Can your technicians work to our SOPs and our forms?
items.a: Yes. If your procedures require your own work order, logbook or calibration forms, we complete those as well as or instead of ours. We send training records with the visit plan, take your site induction and GMP training where you require it, and follow your gowning and permit rules.

items.q: Do you service systems built by another manufacturer?
items.a: Yes, for [makes and equipment types serviced]. No Aquemi serial number is needed: log a service request with the make and model. We start with a condition survey and a review of the drawings, qualification records and spares the system has, because a like-for-like replacement needs a known original. Where records are missing, the survey report lists what to recover before the first planned visit.

items.q: Our IT policy allows no remote access to GMP equipment.
items.a: Then the plan works without it. Remote diagnosis rows in the plan table apply only where you allow read-only telemetry or supervised sessions, and on-site response times are the same either way.

items.q: We have our own maintenance team. Why would we need a plan?
items.a: Many sites keep routine work in-house and buy the parts that need specialist tools or references: USP <645> and <643> calibrations, RO and EDI diagnostics, vent filter integrity testing, the annual system review and fast response on a critical fault. The tier 1 plan is written for that split, and we train your staff on the rest.

items.q: Who signs the service report, and can it go into our batch record review?
items.a: The technician who did the work signs it, and [a second reviewer at Aquemi, to be confirmed] reviews it before issue. It is written to good documentation practice: every value with its unit and limit, every part with its lot number, corrections that leave the original readable. Your quality unit decides what to attach to batch records; the report is laid out so the relevant entries are easy to find.

We use standard parts from named manufacturers wherever the design allows, and the spares list gives the manufacturer and model for each. You can buy them from us or elsewhere; whoever supplies them, the like-for-like check against the qualified bill of materials is the same.

items.q: What happens if you miss a response time?
items.a: [Remedy, e.g. service credit, to be defined.] Each severity 1 response is recorded with the time logged and the time on site, and the annual review shows our response record for your system.

items.q: What does a service plan cost?
items.a: It depends on the system, its age, the number of instruments and your distance from [nearest service base]. Plans start at [lowest plan price, CAD per year]. Send the details below and we return a fixed annual price and the first-visit scope.
